quote: It's just yeah. Being a homeowner is if you don't own a home, it's kinda hard to get that approval.
stewart_read: The rep correctly and promptly names the actual gating requirement (homeownership) right after answering the customer's ZIP-code question. This is accurate DQ procedure, not evasion — the rep didn't dodge the ownership issue, he addressed the customer's literal question first, then stated the rule unprompted.
alternative_hypothesis: One could read the ZIP-code answer at 00:44 as stalling before the DQ, but the very next line shows the rep volunteering the disqualifier without being pushed, which undercuts that reading.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the correct model: answer the customer's actual question, then state the hard requirement plainly. This is a rep behavior to praise, not flag.

quote: Okay. When are you, like, moving in and everything?
stewart_read: After correctly stating the homeownership rule, the rep asks a moving-in question that assumes a standard closing scenario, before the customer has clarified the actual situation is an inherited/family-owned home rather than a pending purchase.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may simply be probing for a timeline to know whether to log a future follow-up, which is reasonable triage, not a knowledge gap.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask an open clarifying question ('what's the situation with the ownership?') before assuming a standard purchase-closing timeline — it would have surfaced the estate/trust complexity a beat sooner.

quote: Do you have any idea what pretty much on his deathbed, and it's everything's in will and trust.
stewart_read: This line is a garbled/merged transcription — it appears to blend rep and customer speech and the attribution is uncertain. If the customer is in fact disclosing that the title-holder (his father-in-law) is terminally ill, that is a vulnerability disclosure that received no acknowledgment in the visible rep response. Given the transcription ambiguity, this should be treated as a possible miss rather than a confirmed one.
alternative_hypothesis: The turn may be a transcription artifact with no discrete customer disclosure to respond to, in which case there is no empathy miss to score — the rep's next line ('I see. I see. Okay.') may already be the full available response to whatever was said.
coaching_implication: Flag for the manager to listen to the raw audio around 01:16-01:23 before treating this as a coaching example — if it confirms a health disclosure, the acknowledge-and-bridge move from coaching_philosophy.empathy_on_vulnerability_disclosure applies; if not, drop it.

quote: What I could do is I could make a note here to maybe reach out to you in a a couple weeks and see if you had any luck with that.
stewart_read: Having correctly identified the DQ, the rep pivots to a vague, self-scheduled callback ('maybe,' 'a couple weeks') with no specific date and no handshake — this is the actual coaching gap on this call, not the DQ handling itself.
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as reasonable pipeline hygiene on a possible future lead, but the vagueness of the offer (and the customer's flat rejection of it) shows it wasn't executed as a real next step.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to either close cleanly on a hard DQ (no callback offered) or, if logging a future-lead note, do it as an internal CRM action rather than a spoken commitment to the customer that invites an on-call rejection.

quote: No. No. No. No. No. No. When the time comes, I will contact whoever I will choose to do the solar panels.
stewart_read: Customer's repeated, emphatic 'no' is a clean and total rejection of any Ion-initiated follow-up, closing the loop on the callback offer the rep made moments earlier.
coaching_implication: This confirms the callback offered at 01:26 was not accepted — the manager should not read this call as having produced any live next step.
